Medium Affected: OTHER

Skytruth Analysis
POLICE RESPONDED TO BURGLAR ALARM AND DISCOVERED HEAVY SMOKE COMING FROM BUILDING. BELTON FIRE DEPT. RESPONDED TO FIND HEAVY FIRE INVOLVING METAL PLATING SOLUTIONS IN DIP TANKS AND ASSOCIATED PIPING. PLATING SOLUTIONS INVOLVED WERE NICKEL SULFARMATE AND SULFURIC ACID (7%). FIRE DEPARTMENT EXTINGUISHED FIRE. MIXTURE OF PLATING SOLUTION AND FIRE FIGHTING WATER COVERED FLOOR OF APPROX. Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT NUMBER 1361510. THE UPDATE IS THEY HAVE CONFIRMED A CATASTROPHIC FAILURE OF A HIGH VOLTAGE TRANSFORMER WHERE THE POWER ENTERS THE MILL CREEK TREATMENT PLANT. A BACK UP TRANSFORMER IS BEING BUILT IN CALIFORNIA AND WONT BE ON SITE FOR AT LEAST TWO WEEKS THEN SEVERAL MORE WEEKS NEEDED TO ASSEMBLE AND TEST. THE OLD FEED WILL HAVE TO BE REBUILT IN ORDER TO RESTORE POWER TO THE PLANT, THIS USUALLY TAKES ONE TO TWO WEEKS. IN THE MEANTIME GENERATORS ARE BEING PLACED ON SITE WITH HE GOAL OF GETTING 130 MGD THROUGH PRIMARY TREATMENT AS SOON AS POSSIBLE AND KEEPING TREATMENT BIOLOGY ALIVE UNTIL SECONDARY TREATMENT CAN BEGIN. A GENERATOR ARRIVED MID AFTERNOON THAT WILL POWER THE MAIN SUPPORT BUILDINGS AND THEY EXPECT TO HAVE ENOUGH CAPACITY ON SITE TOMORROW TO GET PRIMARY TREATMENT RUNNING. ASSESSMENT OF HOW MUCH OF THE CREEK IS BEING AFFECTED BY CSO"S WILL TAKE PLACE TOMORROW. THEY HAVE RELEASED A PRESS RELEASE THAT RECCOMMENDS RECREATION ON THE MILL CREEK AND OHIO RIVER DOWN STREAM OF CINCINNATTI BE AVOIDED./// ///ORIGINAL// THE CALLER STATED THAT A WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT LOST POWER DUE TO A BLOWN TRANSFORMER. BECAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT THE PLANT IS UNABLE TO TREAT ANY WATER, DUE TO THE THE PLANT BEING BYPASSED. THERE IS AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF RAW SEWAGE RELEASING INTO THE MILL CREEK AND THE OHIO RIVER BECAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT.

Skytruth Analysis
INFORMATION RECEIVED VIA WEB REPORT:ON 5/23/06 AT APPROXIMATELY 11:51 AM MST THE ENTIRE PLANT EXPERIENCED AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN AND DEPRESSURIZATION OF THE ENTIRE PROCESSING PLANT TO THE PLANT FLARE STACK. THIS EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF THE FACILITY WAS INITIATED FROM A FIRE IN THE ENGINE/COMPRESSOR BUILDING ON THE # 3 RESIDUE COMPRESSOR ENGINE, WHERE WE HAD A SMALL FIRE ON TOP OF THE ENGINE DRIVER. THE FIRE EYE SAFETY SYSTEM IN THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING SAW THE FIRE AND SHUTDOWN THE ENTIRE FACILITY. THE FIRE STARTED FROM A SMALL AMOUNT OF AMBITROL ENGINE COOLING FLUID ON TOP OF THE ENGINE FROM A RECENT LEAK, THE AMITROL HEATED UP AND FLASHED CAUSING THE SMALL FIRE.

REPORT DATE: 09-20-2024 REPORT TIME: 0946 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: N/A IMAGE DATE: 09-19-2024 IMAGE TIME: 2346 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL1A MODE: INTERFEROMETRIC WIDE (IW) VV RESOLUTION: 5X20 METER LOCATION: 30°18"26" N/86°36"14" W AREA: 0.49 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE SLICK WAS LINEAR IN SHAPE AND APPEARED TO EMANATE FROM THE KNOWN SHIPWRECK (THOMAS HEYWARD), A REPEAT LEAK SOURCE. THE SLICK WAS APPROXIMATELY 3.22NM IN LENGTH, AND APPROXIMATELY 0.08NM AT THE WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE SE AT 8KTS, WHICH ALIGNED WITH THE TRAJECTORY OF THE SLICK. DESPITE THE FACT THAT THE SLICK SEEMED TO BE EMANATING FROM A KNOWN WRECK, IT WAS RELATIVELY FEINT AND HARD TO SEE. FOR THESE REASONS, THE CONFIDENCE FOR THIS REPORT IS MEDIUM-HIGH.
